tables: Cookie
Purpose
Browser lifetime
__Host-thermus-sign-in
Holds temporary sign-in state, a code verifier, return destination, and expiry time to complete sign-in securely.
Up to 10 minutes.
__Host-thermus-session
Holds the encrypted WorkOS session described in section 2, including profile data, access and refresh tokens, and security information.
30 days; this can renew when the session refreshes. WorkOS can end a session earlier.
Hosted information
Retention and deletion handling
Accounts, organizations, memberships, and client authorizations

Keep while needed for active access. Account, membership, and authorization deletion are separate actions. Membership removal alone does not delete the underlying user or unrelated organization access. Apply the operator-action target above to authorized deletion actions.
Initial acceptance and enrollment record

Keep while access is active. Access revocation alone retains the created organization, initial creator agreement metadata, and stable enrollment identifier so repeated signup cannot automatically restore access. Earlier personal-workspace records retain their original schema and purpose. Account deletion receives a separate review of each record and purpose; revocation does not justify indefinite retention. Limit any retained exception to needed evidence or identifiers, with a reason and review date. The record applies to the same WorkOS identity and environment while retained; it does not prevent all future accounts or establish a permanent ban. Deleting this enrollment record can permit a later fresh signup.
Exact documents, agreement wording, and operator records

Keep the exact versioned terms, notice, and agreement wording so initial and separately recorded agreements can be understood. Keep personal acceptance, recovery, privacy-request, and deletion evidence while needed for access, an applicable agreement, a dispute, security, or legal duties. Review need at closure and when a related issue ends. Delete personal information when no longer needed, subject to applicable obligations.
Invitations

Current invitation validity is 7 days. Expiry does not establish deletion of the invitation or delivery records. Cancel invitations no longer needed when closing access and request record deletion where available under the operator-action target above. WorkOS may retain separate operational, security, or legal records.
Service completion, organization-change, operational, and error logs

Render's current plan provides 7 days of accessible application log history. We keep this setting and avoid routine operator-log exports or extra operator-log stores. No Render log-stream destination is currently configured. Organization audit export is a separate stream. Specific security or legal evidence can be retained with a reason and review date. The history window does not establish physical erasure after 7 days or govern provider-managed security, compliance, or backup copies.
Audit destination settings

Keep while needed for the organization’s audit configuration. Disabling export stops export but does not itself delete the destination or saved credential. Thermus does not make a separate backup of these settings or provide a settings restore service. If settings or their encryption key are lost, an Admin may need to re-enter the destination and credential. Authorized deletion requests receive the operator-action review and target above.
Pending audit events and destination copies

Thermus holds pending events only in bounded process memory, with no durable queue, history, or replay. Events can expire or be dropped before delivery. Disabling or changing a destination does not recall copies already sent. The selected destination controls retention and deletion of received copies; contact its operator for those copies.
Provider backups, archives, security, and legal records

Providers retain residual copies under their applicable schedules and legal requirements. We use applicable provider deletion processes. Residual copies can remain after account or membership deletion; no fixed purge deadline for all provider copies is promised.

Organization audit export and destination settings

paragraphs.canonicalText: Save one destination for your organization's audit logs. Thermus system logs are internal.
Enabled export includes tool inputs and results or errors: search queries, requested URLs, fetched text, and reasons. It also includes administration metadata for supported actions.

Thermus redacts recognized credential fields and credential-bearing URL parameters. Event fields exclude sign-in forms, cookies, Authorization headers, and the destination token. Other free text can still contain secrets.
Input and result exports have size limits. Oversized exported results are truncated, with a marker and original and captured sizes in bytes. Your tool results stay complete.

Delivery is best effort. Logs can be lost during overload, outages, or restart, and retries can create duplicates. Thermus provides no audit history or replay. Disabling export cannot recall events already sent.
Send organization data only if you have authority to do so. Check destination access and retention. Read our Privacy Policy.
Settings have no backup. Lost settings may need to be entered again.
For direct Axiom export, use a Bearer token scoped to this dataset. Dataset names use 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, or hyphens. Leave this field blank otherwise.
Leave Token blank to keep a saved Bearer token only when the endpoint and authentication stay the same. A changed endpoint with Bearer needs a new token. None removes the saved token.

Test is optional and sends one synthetic event to the saved destination, even when export is disabled. Save edits before Test. Test does not save settings or enable export. Check your destination for receipt.
Test proves neither continued delivery nor durable storage. Test is not required to enable export.

help.versionEvidence: Help has no rendered version label in supplied JSON; exact canonical hash plus complete ordered text establishes this help revision, not an observed UI version marker

limits: Captured HTML contains both responsive document branches. Full rendered content is compared in each branch, but this is not a fresh desktop/mobile browser layout or interaction observation.
Mobile full notice is inside initially closed details; the complete text exists in the captured HTML. No live expansion or keyboard interaction was performed.
Hyperlink text and targets match the approved renderer. Destination availability and linked external content were not fetched.
Help JSON contains all captured paragraphs, h1 and the Privacy target but has no viewport, geometry or complete heading inventory. It cannot establish deployed mobile/full-page help layout.

The desktop production-destination-disabled.png screenshot was manually viewed: complete What export includes copy is readable; the image ends at the endpoint field and does not show lower form/Test help.
No Terms creator form, new production agreement or acceptance metadata was exercised. The existing-org approved scope remains separate.
No hidden form field, CSRF value, credential, cookie or token is extracted or emitted.

Network provenance and exact deployed commit are manager-supplied capture facts, not independently re-fetched by this offline verification. Privacy HTML itself has no response-header/deployment record in this input.
